title: Holder stability of the vertex-coordinate Dirichlet eigenvalue shape Hessian and its spectrum near a fixed regular polygon with at least five sides
author: Beniamin Bogosel; Dorin Bucur
difficulty_reason: Ordinary domain continuity in H1 does not control the shape-Hessian coefficients, because the material-derivative equations have singular right-hand sides and eigenspace orthogonality constraints. The authors obtain stronger polygon-uniform regularity, estimate the varying right-hand sides and build projection corrections while controlling the material derivatives and coefficient blocks. Those new analytic estimates supply the Holder modulus before the routine finite-dimensional Weyl eigenvalue bound, rather than treating Weyl's theorem as the difficult obligation.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem3.18, fixed n>=5 regular n-gon inscribed in the unit circle and labelled vertex perturbations of sizeepsilon<=epsilon0=(1/4)sin²(pi/n), retaining convexity and uniformly controlled corner angles. The full2n-by2n Hessian of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue in vertex coordinates and its ordered matrix eigenvalues have a common power-modulus continuity bound. Constants depend on fixedn/reference geometry and are only asserted to exist; no optimized/computed minimum neighborhood or numerical positivity claimed. Read complete new distributed second-shape derivative8–12, polygon Hessian/material derivative13–20 and all new geometric continuity22–35, including coupled Whitney/Stein extensions29–31, moving-segment distributions32–33 and projected resolvent estimate34–35. Standard Grisvard corner regularity, Stein extension, Savare-Schimperna domain stability, interpolation and Weyl matrix inequality are identified prior foundations. Source17 proof drops factor2 on one displayed lambdaUiUj term relative to its correct preceding2.18 and original2.1 identity; only continuity of the fully defined Hessian is selected, preserve those displays. Stein extension formula31 has an undefined b in the reference-domain evaluation while its preceding30 construction and following same-distance comparison specify matching averaged evaluations; preserve original formula and construction. Uniform corner regularity is used at a strictly interior positive Sobolev exponent as explicitly allowed in Lemma3.16, no endpoint regularity claim made. Approximate numerical positivity for5–8 sides is stated only up to machine errors4–5 and is not admitted. No polygonal Faber-Krahn conjecture or local minimum claimed proven. historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author couples Stein extension operators for moving corner domains, controls eigenfunctions in higher Sobolev norms and bounds singular segment-supported material-derivative forcing under simultaneous geometric perturbations. These constructions yield continuity of the distributed shape Hessian despite nonsmooth moving vertices, beyond qualifying-exam spectral perturbation theory.
